cases.question: I changed phones and cannot complete MFA. How do I regain payroll access?
cases.reference: Contact the internal Help Desk through an approved corporate channel. After identity verification succeeds, the Help Desk revokes the unavailable authenticator and starts device re-enrolment. A single-use enrolment link is sent to the corporate account and expires after 30 minutes. Register the new device and complete a successful test sign-in; recovery is complete only after that test succeeds. If required verification fails, recovery must stop and be escalated.

trace.question: I changed phones and cannot complete MFA. How do I regain payroll access?
trace.answer:
To regain access to payroll after changing your phone and being unable to complete Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), you need to follow these steps:

1. **Contact the Internal Help Desk**: Reach out through an approved corporate channel. The Help Desk will first verify your identity [SEC-17::standard-recovery-workflow].

2. **Identity Verification**: Be prepared to confirm your identity using two approved factors from your identity record, such as a callback to a registered corporate number or confirmation through a corporate device [SEC-17::identity-verification].

3. **Authenticator Revocation**: Once your identity is verified, the Help Desk will revoke the old authenticator registration and send you a single-use enrolment link to your corporate account [SEC-17::device-re-enrolment]. 

4. **Complete Device Re-enrolment**: Use the enrolment link (which expires after 30 minutes) to register your new device and complete a test sign-in. Recovery is complete only after the test sign-in succeeds [SEC-17::device-re-enrolment].

Make sure not to forward the enrolment link and complete the process promptly.
retrieved_contexts:
[SEC-17::standard-recovery-workflow]
Document: Payroll MFA Recovery Policy (version 2.1)
Section: Standard recovery workflow
The employee must contact the internal Help Desk through an approved corporate channel. The Help Desk first verifies identity, then revokes the unavailable authenticator, and finally starts device re-enrolment. The employee must complete the new enrolment before normal payroll access is restored. If any required verification fails, the Help Desk must stop the recovery and escalate the case.

[SEC-17::device-re-enrolment]
Document: Payroll MFA Recovery Policy (version 2.1)
Section: Device re-enrolment
After successful verification, the Help Desk revokes the old authenticator registration and issues a single-use enrolment link to the employee's corporate account. The link expires after 30 minutes and must not be forwarded. The employee registers the new device and completes a test sign-in. Recovery is complete only after the test sign-in succeeds.

[SEC-17::identity-verification]
Document: Payroll MFA Recovery Policy (version 2.1)
Section: Identity verification
Before changing MFA, the Help Desk must verify the employee identifier and two approved factors from the identity record. Approved factors may include a callback to a registered corporate number, confirmation through the signed-in corporate device, or an in-person identity check. The technician must never request the employee's password, one-time passcode, full national identity number, or personal banking PIN.
